verdict: Caution — lend selectively to owner-run mid-market hotels and F&B with verified bed capacity and cash cover; avoid leveraged new capex and unregistered small stays until the municipal survey data is in hand.
title: Dehradun Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Dehradun hotel turns rooms, beds and kitchen covers into nightly cash, and the cash arrives before most costs are paid.** Guests prepay or pay at checkout; staff, power, laundry and food suppliers are paid on 15-30 day cycles; the owner's real capital sits in the building, the furniture and the licence. So when a proposal lands, check the bed count and the licence first, not the projected occupancy. The municipal corporation is now compiling exactly this — hotel names, addresses and bed capacity across the city [2]. **That survey is your best free underwriting tool; ask every applicant for their filed bed count and match it to the property.**

## Where value and cash actually sit
**Pricing power in Dehradun is seasonal and thin, so the value sits in the land and the repeat guest book, not the tariff.** Room revenue swings with the Char Dham and Mussoorie leisure flow; F&B is steadier but lower-margin. Working capital is short — receivables are mostly OTA and corporate payouts, so the cycle is weeks, not months. Capex is the killer: a room refurbishment or a banquet hall is lumpy and irreversible. **So structure term debt to the asset, not to the season, and never fund furniture out of a cash-credit line.** Where the applicant cannot show us the split between room, F&B and banquet revenue, write 'collect from customer'.

## What has changed now
**The local news is thin and mostly about access, not demand.** A new bus service on the Vikasnagar–Chakrata–Mussoorie route is being positioned as a tourism boost [1]; that widens the feeder catchment but tells us nothing about room rates. The bed-capacity survey [2] signals formalisation — unregistered small stays will face scrutiny. Peer results are strong but national, not local: ITC Hotels posted consolidated revenue of Rs 1,054 crore, up 26 percent, with EBITDA up 37 percent [4]; Leela's Q2 was driven by 30 percent RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led [6]; Ventive's international occupancy stood at 71 percent [5]. **Read these as proof that branded, well-run inventory is pricing up — not as evidence about a 20-room property on Rajpur Road.** The ICRA hotel methodology [8] and the CHL rational report [9] are undated here; treat them as framework, not current fact.

Take a mortgage on the property, a personal guarantee, and a DSRA of a few months' EMI. **Every month, take the GST return, the OTA payout statement and the electricity bill — the power bill is the hardest number to fake.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the gap between billed occupancy and power consumption; a widening gap means rooms are being sold off-book or not at all.** Watch OTA payout delays and any shift from prepaid to credit corporate billing. Watch staff attrition and unpaid supplier cheques. If the municipal survey flags a property as unregistered [2], stop new limits until it is regularised.
watch: billed occupancy falls below filed bed capacity by a wide margin -> ask for OTA statements and re-rate limit
payout delays beyond normal cycle -> move to cash-collateralised structure
property unregistered or bed count mismatched -> freeze new limits until regularised
DSRA drawn twice in a year -> escalate to restructuring review
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Bus route aids access; bed survey formalises stock; peer growth is national, not Dehradun-specific.
